issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as both messageOnFeed() (UML and Part 1) and getFeedingSound() (Part 2 and feedAllAnimals description). The provided solution and intended template structure use messageOnFeed(), so the conflicting name getFeedingSound() in the problem text will confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem text with messageOnFeed(), or alternatively change the abstract method name in the UML/template/solution to getFeedingSound(). Update the descriptions that mention feedAllAnimals() to call the same method name used in the class API.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method using two different identifiers: messageOnFeed() (declared as the abstract method in the Animal description) and getFeedingSound() (used in the per-animal requirements for Seal, Pig, and Goat). The provided solution and expected template implementation use messageOnFeed(). This discrepancy can confuse students about which method to implement and which name to call when feeding animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the feeding-method identifier consistent across artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to use messageOnFeed() everywhere (replace getFeedingSound() occurrences), or alternatively add a clear note that getFeedingSound() is an alias for messageOnFeed(). Prefer using messageOnFeed() to match the abstract method declared in Animal and the solution implementation.
